content.text: The text reviews gastric cancer: progressive cachexia, anemia, emaciation, edema, thrombosis, fever, dyspnea, rare dyspnoeic coma, hepatic/peritoneal metastases, fistulas, complications, pathology, diagnosis, prognosis, and largely palliative treatment. A fairly nourished elderly man was found comatose in the streets and brought to Bellevue Hospital; autopsy revealed gastric cancer without diabetes. It then discusses gastric hemorrhage, its causes and differentiation from hemoptysis; gastric dilatation from pyloric obstruction or atony, its signs, diagnosis, prognosis, and lavage-based treatment; cirrhosis, hypertrophic pyloric stenosis, atrophy, rupture, and gastromalacia. Finally, intestinal indigestion and constipation are attributed to dietary, functional, systemic, or obstructive causes, producing bloating, altered stools, malnutrition, and nervous symptoms; treatment emphasizes diet, exercise, regular habits, enemas, and cautious laxatives.
